$comment: Cross-runtime vectors for the one gRPC status detail the internal RPC surface defines outside the .proto files (RB-A23). Producer: Control (anvilkit.control.v1). Consumer: the API. A revision conflict that knows both revisions answers gRPC ABORTED with its unchanged message (`REVISION_CONFLICT: ` and the conflict's text) and exactly one google.rpc.ErrorInfo detail: reason `REVISION_CONFLICT`, domain `anvilkit.control.v1`, metadata `expectedRevision` and `currentRevision`, each a canonical unsigned 64-bit decimal (no sign, no leading zero, no whitespace). The consumer copies both values to the public error's details.expectedRevision and details.currentRevision only from a detail with that reason and domain whose two values are both canonical; it ignores other metadata keys, and any other detail, or none, yields no public revisions. The message, the gRPC code and the public code never depend on the detail, so a peer that predates it loses only the two values. Each `detail` is the ProtoJSON form of google.rpc.ErrorInfo; `revisions` is what the consumer must copy (null: nothing); `produced` says whether the producer emits exactly this detail for those revisions. tools/check.py (Python) and tests/go (Go) decide every case by the rule above; Control and the API test against verbatim copies of this file (the parent's tools/check-contracts.py compares them byte for byte).

cases.name: the uint64 maximum and zero are revisions
an unknown metadata key beside two canonical revisions is ignored
a leading zero is not canonical
a value above the uint64 maximum is no revision
a non-numeric value is no revision
an empty value is no revision
one revision without the other is copied as neither
a detail without metadata carries no revisions
another owner's domain is not Control's conflict
another reason is not a revision conflict
